newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian pilots call off protest.
newsitem.headline: Indian pilots call off protest.

text.p: Pilots of India's state-owned Indian Airlines called off a three-day old protest over job benefits on Monday after the stoppage left hundreds of travellers stranded, the United News of India (UNI) said.
UNI quoted officials of the Indian Commercial Pilots Association (ICPA) as saying the pilots decided to return to work after certain "assurances from the management".
The suspension of five pilots by the domestic airline's management on Saturday was also revoked as part of the deal, UNI said.

At least 22 flights were cancelled on Friday and seven on Saturday as at least 92 pilots stayed home to back demands for fixed flying-hours allowances, free meals during layovers, and other benefits. Some of the flights resumed on Sunday.
Airline officials had said a wage agreement with the pilots was not up for re-negotiation until December 1998.
